title: Team formation reset: clear teams when anyone leaves, and let the organizer delete teams
description:
Product decision from mobile manual testing 2026-10-04 (mobile tickets mobile-app-a01.21 and the reset rule). Observed: on session c588f245 everyone left except the creator and the session still has its 2 drafted teams; there is no endpoint to delete teams (only POST /teams, draft and proposal routes).

Wanted behaviour: a full RESET of team formation = the session goes back to its initial state, 'like there was never any draft':
- delete the session's teams and team_config (everyone unassigned),
- cancel a running captain draft and an open voting round (new cancel reason, e.g. roster_changed / teams_reset), proposals removed,
- clients must no longer see the old draft as the 'latest draft' (GET /sessions/{id}/draft -> 404 or a reset marker), because mobile only offers 'Propose teams' when there was no draft or the latest was cancelled; after a reset proposals must be allowed again.

Triggers:
1) Automatically whenever a confirmed attendee (going/promoted) stops holding a spot: cancels their RSVP (DELETE /rsvp), switches to maybe/not_going, or is removed by a manager. 'Always restart' — any leaver resets, not just team members. (This replaces today's AttendeeLeft behaviour of removing them from the draft pool / proposals and the leaver-only team unassign.)
2) Manually: new organizer endpoint, e.g. DELETE /api/v1/sessions/{id}/teams (canManageSession; 409 if session canceled/completed), same reset.

Also: emit a stream update (snapshot with no teams/draft/voting) and decide notifications (probably notify people who were on teams that teams were reset). Open question for product: should a new joiner also reset teams? (Not requested; today they stay unassigned.)
acceptance_criteria: Any confirmed attendee leaving/removed/stepping down to maybe resets teams, draft and voting to the initial state; organizer can do the same via the new endpoint; GET /draft no longer reports the old draft; stream snapshot reflects it; tests.
notes: Product decision 2026-10-04: a new joiner does NOT reset teams (they stay unassigned) - for now.
close_reason: Team formation reset: any confirmed attendee leaving (cancel RSVP, maybe/not_going, removed) or DELETE /sessions/{id}/teams deletes teams, cancels draft/vote, clears draft+vote history; teams_reset event + team_formation_reset notification; joiners do not reset

title: Add geocoding proxy/cache service for Nominatim (replace direct mobile->Nominatim calls)
description:
## Problem

The mobile app currently calls https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org directly from the client to resolve lat/long <-> City/Country. This has several downsides:

- No control over Nominatim's usage policy (max 1 req/sec, requires a valid User-Agent/Referer, no heavy uniform polling) - risk of the app's IP/traffic getting rate-limited or blocked since all requests originate from many individual mobile clients instead of one identifiable backend.
- No caching - repeated lookups for the same City/Country (or the same lat/long bucket) always hit Nominatim again, wasting quota and adding latency for users.
- No observability - we cannot trace, meter, or alert on geocoding calls the way we do for our own services (OpenTelemetry/Prometheus).
- Mobile team is coupled to a third-party API contract directly (shape of Nominatim responses leaks into the app).
- Nominatim/OSM usage policy requires attribution and a proper User-Agent identifying the application - easy to get wrong when called from many client installs, easy to enforce centrally from one backend service.

## Proposed solution

Introduce a new backend service (working name: `location` or `geocoding`) that sits between mobile and Nominatim:

```
mobile -> gateway -> location-service -> nominatim -> location-service -> mobile
```

Responsibilities:
1. Expose our own REST endpoints (via the gateway, following the existing routing/auth pattern in gateway/internal) for:
   - Reverse geocoding: lat/long -> City/Country (and any other fields the app needs).
   - (Optional/forward-looking) Forward geocoding: City/Country -> lat/long, if/when mobile needs it.
2. Proxy requests to Nominatim's API on the backend, setting a proper User-Agent per Nominatim's usage policy and enforcing our own outbound rate limiting (mirroring Nominatim's max 1 req/sec policy) so we don't get blocked.
3. Cache results in PostgreSQL (or Redis, see open questions) keyed by normalized City+Country (and/or rounded lat/long) so repeated lookups for the same location don't hit Nominatim again.
4. Follow existing service conventions from CLAUDE.md "Adding a New Service": DDD layering (domain/application/infrastructure/interfaces), own cmd entrypoint, own migration(s) for the cache table, registered in gateway router, added to docker-compose.yaml, service-specific Prometheus metrics.

## Why this matters / priority

- Direct third-party calls from a mobile client are a latent production risk: if Nominatim rate-limits or blocks our traffic (shared IP ranges, missing/invalid User-Agent, bursty usage), reverse-geocoding breaks for all users with no server-side fallback or visibility.
- This is straightforward to introduce now (before the mobile app has many more direct integration points against Nominatim) and unlocks caching, cost/latency savings, and observability.

## Scope / Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New service scaffolded following existing DDD conventions (domain/application/infrastructure/interfaces + metrics), with its own cmd entrypoint.
- [ ] Endpoint(s) for reverse geocoding (lat/long -> City/Country) exposed through the gateway, following existing auth/routing rules.
- [ ] Outbound calls to Nominatim set a compliant User-Agent and respect Nominatim's usage policy (rate limiting to <= 1 req/sec).
- [ ] Results are cached (DB table or Redis) keyed by normalized location, with a defined TTL/invalidation strategy, so repeat lookups for the same City/Country avoid a new Nominatim call.
- [ ] Service registered in docker-compose.yaml and gateway router.
- [ ] Basic Prometheus metrics for the new service (request counts/latency, cache hit/miss ratio, Nominatim call counts).
- [ ] Mobile team has a documented contract (endpoint + request/response shape) to switch to, replacing their direct Nominatim calls.

## Open questions (to resolve during design/implementation)

- Cache store: shared PostgreSQL table (consistent with "shared DB across services" pattern) vs. Redis (already used for caching elsewhere)?
- Cache key normalization strategy: exact City+Country string match vs. rounded lat/long grid buckets vs. both.
- TTL for cached entries (Nominatim data can change, e.g. new addresses) - or treat City/Country resolution as effectively immutable and cache indefinitely.
- Whether to also cover forward geocoding (City/Country -> lat/long) now or in a follow-up.
- New service name/port and whether it lives under an existing bounded context (e.g. account-profile, since it's used for user location context) or as a standalone service.
close_reason: Location service implemented (commit e233b69): reverse+forward geocoding via gateway, Nominatim UA + 1 req/s limiter, Postgres bucket cache, metrics, compose, swagger and README contract. All acceptance criteria verified in code.

title: ReconstructActivityGroup drops capacity - GetActivityGroupByID always returns nil DefaultCapacity, so group capacity is never enforced
description:
activity/internal/domain/activity_group.go's ReconstructActivityGroup(id, creatorID, title, description, activityType, difficultyLevel, visibility, status, location, timezone, capacity, createdAt, updatedAt, cancelledAt, deletedAt) *ActivityGroup accepts a capacity *Capacity parameter but never assigns it in the returned &ActivityGroup{...} struct literal - the capacity field is simply omitted, so it's left at its zero value (nil) regardless of what's passed in.

activity_group_repo.go's GetActivityGroupByID (and mapActivityGroupModelToDomain) correctly scans default_capacity from the DB and constructs a non-nil *domain.Capacity when the column is non-NULL, then passes it into ReconstructActivityGroup - but that value is silently discarded. Confirmed via a debug test: creating an ActivityGroup with capacity=1 and immediately calling GetActivityGroupByID on it returns group.DefaultCapacity() == nil.

Impact: every capacity check in member_service.go (RequestToJoin's up-front check and ApproveMember's re-check, both guarded by 'if capacity := group.DefaultCapacity(); capacity != nil') is unconditionally skipped for ANY activity group loaded from the database, since GetActivityGroupByID is the only way application code loads a persisted group. This means activity group capacity limits have never been enforced at runtime - not a concurrency bug, a total no-op, independent of the TOCTOU race fixed for group capacity in rekreativko-api-b8q (which cannot even be verified/exercised until this is fixed, since the capacity-check block itself never runs).

Fix: add capacity: capacity, to the &ActivityGroup{...} struct literal in ReconstructActivityGroup.
close_reason: ReconstructActivityGroup was silently dropping its capacity parameter instead of assigning it to the struct, so GetActivityGroupByID always returned nil DefaultCapacity and group capacity was never enforced regardless of concurrency. Fixed by assigning capacity: capacity in the struct literal; verified via a debug test that round-trips a group through create+load.

title: CreateRSVP capacity downgrade is dead code for non-approval 'going' RSVPs
description: In activity/internal/application/attendee_service.go's CreateRSVP, the non-approval 'going' branch calls domain.NewRSVPManualAttendee(session, groupID, userID, status) which sets a.status = status (i.e. AttendeeStatusGoing) immediately, then calls attendee.UpdateRSVP(status, session, confirmedCount) to apply the capacity-aware downgrade-to-pending logic. But domain.Attendee.UpdateRSVP's very first line is 'if newStatus == a.status { return nil // no change }' - since a.status is already Going (set by NewRSVPManualAttendee above) and newStatus is also Going, this check is always true, so UpdateRSVP returns immediately without ever running the hasCapacity check. Net effect: a brand-new RSVP to a non-approval-gated session for status='going' is ALWAYS created as 'going', regardless of session capacity - overbooking every full session's non-approval-gated 'going' RSVP path, independent of any concurrency (this is a sequential logic bug, not the TOCTOU race fixed in rekreativko-api-b48, though it compounds it). The capacity check only actually works today via UpdateRSVP (an existing attendee changing status to going, where oldStatus != Going) and via CreateRSVP's approval-gated branch (a separate HasCapacity check before creating a pending join request). Fix: in CreateRSVP's non-approval branch, create the attendee with an initial status of Pending (or via a status-less constructor) and then call UpdateRSVP(status, session, confirmedCount) to let it decide the real starting status, OR check capacity before calling NewRSVPManualAttendee and pass in AttendeeStatusPending directly when the session is full.
close_reason: Made NewRSVPManualAttendee check capacity itself for status=Going (downgrading to Pending + emitting AutoPendingEvent when full) instead of relying on a follow-up UpdateRSVP call that was always a no-op since newStatus already equaled the just-constructed status. Verified with unit tests that fail without the fix.

title: Gateway API key secret committed in observability/prometheus.yml
description: The real GATEWAY_API_KEY value used to protect service-to-service auth (shared/middleware/gateway_key.go CheckGatewayKey) and the gateway /metrics endpoint (shared/middleware/metrics_auth.go RequireMetricsToken) is hardcoded in plaintext at observability/prometheus.yml:34 (credentials: "468019b5-a863-4e49-b8d8-2c420079ac7b"). This value is identical to GATEWAY_API_KEY / GATEWAY_API_KEYS in the gitignored .env file (.env:28-29), confirming it is the live secret, not a placeholder. The file's own comment (observability/prometheus.yml:26-29) explicitly warns 'in production this file must not be checked in with a real secret inlined - inject it via templating or a secret-mounted config,' but the real secret was committed anyway in commit 36cb6607. Anyone with read access to the git history/repo now has the key that authenticates as the gateway to every backend service (identity, account-profile, activity, notifications) and can also scrape the gateway's own /metrics. Fix: rotate GATEWAY_API_KEY/GATEWAY_API_KEYS immediately, remove the literal value from prometheus.yml (use envsubst/templating at container start, or a Prometheus secret file via file_sd/external secret mount), and scrub the value from git history if feasible.
close_reason: Removed hardcoded GATEWAY_API_KEY from observability/prometheus.yml; switched to credentials_file backed by a Docker Compose secret, rotated the key in .env

title: Mising visibility paramater in CresteSessionRequest
description: Mobile team currently sends two requests to when creating new Sessions. One to create and other to update visibility. We MUST give them option to send visibility in one request and do it in one request. Check if same must be done for update session
close_reason: Added visibility to CreateSessionRequest/UpdateSessionRequest (now required on both), wired through to domain SetVisibility/NewSession, and removed the standalone-must-be-public restriction so standalone sessions can be public or private.

title: GET /sessions/{id}/attendees has no requester check and returns pending/waitlisted people to anyone
description: ListAttendees (interfaces/http/attendee_handler.go) -> AttendeeService.ListRSVPs takes no requester: it neither checks that the caller may see the session (a private session's attendee list is readable by anyone who has its id) nor limits non-managers to confirmed attendees, so pending join requests and the waitlist are returned to every authenticated caller. Mobile's backend-api-contract.md has an attendee-list privacy note that the endpoint does not enforce. Fix: pass the requester, require session visibility (404 otherwise), and for non-managers return only confirmed (going/promoted) attendees, or filter status to that set; managers keep the full list. Acceptance: tests for a private session (404 for a stranger), a public session (non-manager sees only going/promoted), and a manager (sees pending). Found while fixing rekreativko-api-egw (same data leaked on the SSE stream).
close_reason: GET /attendees needs session visibility (404 otherwise); non-managers get only going/promoted (own row exempt), managers get everyone; repo Statuses filter

title: SSE stream leaks pending join requests to non-managers (raw attendee.join_requested event)
description: The team-formation stream sends the raw domain event to every connected viewer as 'change' (hub.go: Update{Change: json.RawMessage(payload)}), with no filtering by event type or viewer role. attendee.join_requested carries user_id (the requester) and manager_user_ids, so on a public session any viewer with the stream open learns who asked to join and who the managers are, contradicting the rule that pending requests are visible to managers only. Other attendee events (join_approved/join_rejected) are likely affected too. Fix options: drop or redact attendee.join_* events for non-managers (the hub would need a per-viewer manager check, cached), or strip user_id/manager_user_ids from 'change' for those events; non-managers could simply receive no change payload for them. Acceptance: a non-manager viewer's stream never contains a pending requester's id or the manager list; managers still get the events; test with a public session. Found while checking mobile ticket rekreativko-api-6gg.13.
close_reason: Stream filters per viewer: join_requested/join_rejected/auto_pending/rsvp_auto_pending only to managers and the subject; manager_user_ids stripped for non-managers; fails closed

title: Team-formation stream: push RSVP changes (join, maybe, leave) for the session
description:
Found in mobile manual testing 2026-10-04 (mobile-app-1in). The team-formation SSE stream only fires on draft/voting/team changes. When someone joins, switches to maybe, or leaves without being on a team, other viewers' Teams card (its Unassigned pool) and attendee list stay stale until they refetch — mobile currently relies on polling/refetch for that.

Wanted: emit a stream event on attendee status changes for the session (e.g. attendee.joined, attendee.status_changed, attendee.left) and include the confirmed (going/promoted) attendee ids in the team-formation snapshot, so a client can render teams + the unassigned pool from one document without a separate attendee fetch. Respect the existing visibility/privacy rules (no pending join requests to non-managers — see the attendee-list privacy note in mobile's backend-api-contract.md).
acceptance_criteria: Joining, switching to maybe/going and leaving each push a stream event; the snapshot carries the confirmed attendee ids; no pending-request data leaks to non-managers; tests.
notes: Backend check 2026-10-04 (code, not run live): the premise 'the stream says nothing on RSVP changes' is not right. activity/internal/interfaces/live/hub.go subscribes to activity.session.> and pushes a snapshot for EVERY session event, so attendee.rsvp_going / rsvp_maybe / rsvp_not_going / promoted / removed / auto_confirmed already arrive as named events with {change, snapshot}; 'change' carries user_id. The real gap: TeamFormationSnapshot (application/team_formation_query.go) has no attendee list, so the pushed snapshot looks unchanged. Corrected scope: add confirmed (going/promoted) attendee ids to the snapshot, shared by GET /team-formation and the stream. Privacy: do it together with the join_requested leak ticket, because the same stream already exposes pending requests to non-managers.
close_reason: Snapshot carries going_user_ids (going/promoted only) for GET /team-formation and the stream; RSVP events already pushed; privacy via egw

title: Team proposals: refuse proposals once teams were set by a captain draft
description:
Product rule from mobile (mobile-app-a01.20, 2026-10-04): teams picked in a captain draft are not put to a vote. Mobile now offers 'Propose teams' only when the session never had a draft or its latest draft was cancelled (draftAllowsProposals). Backend today only refuses during a running draft (409 draft_already_active), so a completed draft still lets anyone POST /sessions/{id}/proposals directly.

Wanted: POST /proposals returns 409 (e.g. teams_drafted) when the session's current teams came from a completed captain draft. After a team reset (rekreativko-api-6gg.11: someone leaves, or the organizer deletes teams) proposals are allowed again. Edge to decide: a re-draft that gets cancelled leaves the earlier drafted teams in place — those are still drafted teams, so proposals should stay refused (track where the current teams came from, e.g. session.teams_source = draft|vote, rather than looking only at the latest draft). Ideally expose that on the session/team-formation snapshot so the client can use it instead of inferring from GET /draft.
acceptance_criteria: POST /proposals is refused while the current teams come from a completed draft (including after a cancelled re-draft) and allowed again after a reset; the teams' origin is exposed to clients; tests.
close_reason: teams_source (manual|draft|vote) on the session: POST /proposals is 409 teams_drafted while the current teams came from a completed draft (incl. after a cancelled re-draft); allowed after reset/manual/vote; exposed on the snapshot

title: Team voting: let a voter retract their vote
description:
Requested by mobile (mobile-app-a01.17, found in manual testing 2026-10-04). Today a vote can only be moved to another option (PUT /sessions/{id}/proposals/vote); there is no way back to 'not voted'. With one proposal and no keep_current option the vote is effectively locked.

Proposed: DELETE /api/v1/sessions/{id}/proposals/vote — the caller's own vote, while the round is open. Domain: TeamVotingRound.RetractVote(voterID) (delete from votes, version++, event). Errors: 409 voting_closed (no open round / closed / cancelled), 404 or no-op if the caller has no vote (decide; mobile prefers idempotent 200), 409 attendee_not_going if not confirmed. Returns the voting state (same DTO as GET /proposals, my_vote null). Emit a stream update so other viewers' tallies refresh (voting.vote_retracted or reuse vote_cast).
acceptance_criteria: A voter can remove their vote while voting is open; tallies/votes_cast update and the stream notifies viewers; closed rounds reject it; integration test for the repo path.

title: Gateway forwards client-supplied X-User-ID on public routes
description:
gateway/internal/router.go addUserHeaders only SETS X-User-ID when the caller is authenticated; it never removes a header the client sent. On public routes (login, register, verify-account, resend-verification-code, refresh-token) there is no authenticated user, so a client-supplied X-User-ID passes through to identity unchanged, and identity's middleware.ExtractUserContext puts that id into the request context as the account id.

Not exploitable today: the identity handlers that read the account id (GetCurrentAccount, DeleteCurrentAccount, LogoutHandler) are on protected routes, where the gateway overwrites the header with the JWT's account. But any future public endpoint that reads authcontext.GetAccountID would let anyone act as any user.

Fix: always delete the incoming X-User-ID before setting it from the authenticated context, so only the gateway can set it. Test that a spoofed header never reaches the backend on an unauthenticated request and is replaced on an authenticated one.
close_reason: Gateway always drops client-sent X-User-ID before setting it from the auth context; covered by router test

title: Standalone session creator cannot complete their own session (Session.Complete checks group role only)
description: domain.Session.Complete checks requesterRole.CanManageMembers() (group creator/admin) instead of s.canManageSession(requesterID, requesterRole) like Start and Cancel do. A standalone session has no group, so the handler passes an empty role and POST /sessions/{id}/complete always fails with unauthorized for its creator - the only way it ever completes is the expiry cron, and only if it has an end_time. It also means a group admin who is not the session creator is allowed but the session's own creator in a group is only allowed via their group role. Fix: use canManageSession in Complete (and add requesterID to the check), plus a domain unit test for standalone and group sessions. Found while writing integration tests for rekreativko-api-6gg.7 (test had to pass role 'creator' explicitly). Effort: S.
close_reason: Session.Complete uses canManageSession so a standalone session's creator can complete it

title: Cancelling an activity group does not cancel its sessions (Session.CancelFromGroup is never called)
description: ActivityGroupService.CancelActivityGroup only cancels the group aggregate. domain.Session.CancelFromGroup(reason, attendeeUserIDs) exists but has no caller anywhere, so a cancelled group's scheduled/started sessions stay live: attendees are not told (no activity.session.cancelled fan-out), the sessions still show in listings, and any running captain draft or open team voting round on them keeps running. Fix: cascade the group cancel to its scheduled/started sessions - in the same transaction or via an activity.group.cancelled consumer - and for each session take the session lock, call CancelFromGroup and teamFormation.sessionEnded (added in rekreativko-api-6gg.7) so draft/voting end with session_ended. Needs an integration test. Effort: M.
close_reason: Group cancel cascades in-tx: live sessions CancelFromGroup + draft/voting session_ended; generator skips cancelled/deleted groups

title: Team size is a minimum: players_per_team -> min_players_per_team, no team_full (mobile D1-D3)
description:
Mobile product decisions (Team Formation Backend Asks page, 2026-09-26):
- D1: players_per_team means 'at least this many per team to play', no upper limit. Rename to min_players_per_team (POST /sessions/{id}/teams request, team_config in session responses, teams_created event). A team is never full: PUT .../rsvp/{userId}/team drops the size check and the team_full error.
- D2: everyone going is on a team; no substitutes; uneven teams allowed.
- D3: 'enough people' = team_count x min_players_per_team (or 1 per team when unset). Checked only where flows need it (draft start, proposals, voting) - manual assignment and POST /teams are never blocked by it. New error not_enough_players (409).
Schema: session.players_per_team -> min_players_per_team (edit 000001, no new migration).
acceptance_criteria: min_players_per_team in API/events/schema; no team_full anywhere; D3 helper on TeamConfig used by draft start; tests updated
close_reason: Team size is a minimum: min_players_per_team (API/events/schema), no max check or team_full; TeamConfig.PlayersNeeded/HasEnoughPlayers for D3

title: Teams are created after people join, not at session creation
description:
6gg.1 made team config part of POST /sessions (fixed at creation) and of session templates. The real workflow is: 1) session created, 2) people join until full, 3) creator/admin creates teams and fills them. Rework:
- Remove teams from POST /sessions and from session templates (domain, repo, schema columns, DTOs, generator inheritance, template service groupRepo).
- New POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/teams {team_count (default 2), players_per_team?, colors?} by session creator or group admin/creator, team sports only, any time while scheduled/started (not tied to 'full').
- Creating teams when they already exist REPLACES them: all attendees unassigned (team_unassigned, reason teams_replaced), old teams deleted, new empty Team A/B/... created. Under the session advisory lock.
- Event activity.session.teams_created. session.team_count/players_per_team now set by this step.
- Existing assign/unassign, slot release and team events unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Sessions and templates are created without teams; POST /sessions/{id}/teams creates or replaces teams (assignments cleared) for team sports; assign endpoint works on the created teams; tests, swagger, activity.md updated
close_reason: Teams are created via POST /sessions/{id}/teams after people join (replace unassigns everyone); removed teams from session creation and templates

title: Session invitee cannot view a private standalone session before accepting the invite
description: SessionService.GetSession only shows a private session to its creator, attendees or confirmed group members (isSessionRelated). A user with a pending session invite (rekreativko-api-06r) is none of those, so the client can show the invite (which only carries session_id) but cannot fetch the session's title/time/location to let them decide whether to accept. Consider treating a pending, unexpired session invite as 'related' in isSessionRelated (needs SessionInviteRepository in SessionService), or embedding a session summary in SessionInviteResponse. Also check ListSessions/DiscoverSessions visibility.
close_reason: Pending unexpired session invite counts as related: invitee can GetSession/ListSessions a private session before accepting

title: Notifications: handle activity.session_invite.* events
description: Session invites (rekreativko-api-06r) publish activity.session_invite.sent/accepted/declined/expired via the outbox, but the notifications service only subscribes to activity.invite.* (group invites), so an invitee is never told they were invited (only discoverable by polling GET /api/v1/session-invites) and the creator isn't told about accept/decline/expiry. Add subscriber entries + handlers in notifications/internal/interfaces/events (mirror inviteSent/Accepted/Declined/Expired handlers, payload has session_id instead of activity_id), new notification types, and handler tests.
close_reason: Notifications subscribe to activity.session_invite.* and create session_invite_sent/accepted/declined/expired notifications

title: Live updates for team formation via SSE (server->client stream)
description:
DECISION: use Server-Sent Events (SSE). Commands (assign, pick, propose, vote, close) stay plain REST; the stream only tells clients that state changed. Mobile team leaned WebSocket (React Native has no built-in EventSource; polyfill needed on native and web) - we chose SSE anyway, revisit WebSocket later if needed (e.g. chat/live scoring). Keep the hub/snapshot design transport-agnostic so switching only touches the last handler.

## Scope
One stream per session carrying ALL team-formation state: captain draft (turns, picks, completed/cancelled), proposals + vote tallies, voting closed / tie needs admin, and team assignment changes (from draft, vote result or direct admin assignment). Does NOT carry RSVPs, attendee joins/leaves or session edits (may be added later).

## Design
- Endpoint: GET /activity/api/v1/sessions/{id}/events, Accept: text/event-stream, normal Authorization header, proxied through the gateway like any other route. Note: browser-native EventSource cannot set Authorization; the RN web build must use a fetch-based SSE client/polyfill.
- Access check on connect: same visibility rule as reading the session (Session.IsVisibleTo / confirmed attendee).
- Every event is a full snapshot of team-formation state (current teams + draft if any + open proposals with tallies). First event on connect is a snapshot, so reconnect = fresh snapshot; no Last-Event-ID replay or delta merging. Include a monotonically increasing id/version so clients can ignore stale snapshots.
- Heartbeat comment line (": ping") every 15-25s.
- Source: outbox -> NATS -> each activity API instance subscribes and fans out through an in-memory hub keyed by session id -> connected clients.
- GET snapshot endpoint returns the same payload (client fallback: poll every 2-3s if SSE misbehaves on a platform).

## Must fix / verify in current code (nothing streaming exists today)
- gateway/cmd/api/main.go:185 http.Server WriteTimeout 15s and activity/cmd/api/main.go:245 WriteTimeout 15s will kill the stream: clear the write deadline per request for this route (http.ResponseController).
- gateway/internal/proxy.go ProxyToService wraps every request in a per-service context timeout (default 30s, ACTIVITY_SERVICE_TIMEOUT): bypass for the stream route.
- Verify middleware chain (metrics, tracing/otelhttp, logging wrappers) preserves http.Flusher / Unwrap so events are not buffered.
- Measure outbox publisher polling interval: it adds to end-to-end latency between a pick/vote and clients seeing it.
- Consider closing/filtering the stream if a user is removed from the session mid-stream.

## Client notes (mobile)
Open only while the draft/vote screen is visible; background delivery is push (separate epic). Client refetches full state on reconnect.
acceptance_criteria: Clients receive team-formation snapshots in near real time through the gateway; heartbeat keeps idle connections alive; reconnect gets a fresh snapshot; unauthorized users rejected; stream not cut by gateway/activity timeouts; tested across multiple API instances
notes: Mobile decisions (2026-09-26, D17-D20): D17 SSE at GET /activity/api/v1/sessions/{id}/events with the normal Authorization header (fetch-based client on native+web), heartbeats, full snapshot on connect and every change. D18 ONE snapshot document identical from the stream and a GET: teams + draft state (6gg.2 shape) + proposals list (6gg.3 shape) + version - publish this shape first, screens are built from it. D19 server closes the stream when the access token expires; reconnect with the expired token -> 401; users removed from the session are disconnected. D20 each event carries what changed (player_picked, vote_cast, voting_closed, ...) with the ids involved, alongside the snapshot.

title: Team formation events as in-app notifications
description:

title: Captain draft: admin picks two captains, captains alternately pick players
description:
Draft state machine per session.
- Admin/creator picks two captains from joined (confirmed) attendees and starts the draft.
- Turn order + current turn stored; captain may only pick an unassigned confirmed attendee on their own turn (reject otherwise).
- Captains are auto-assigned to their teams. Draft completes when all confirmed attendees are assigned; result written to team_id (replaces previous teams - admin-initiated).
- Admin can cancel a draft; existing teams remain untouched on cancel.
- Edge cases: captain leaves/goes not_going mid-draft, attendee leaves mid-draft, waitlist promotion mid-draft, turn timeout (decide alternate vs snake and timeout).
- Events: draft_started, turn_changed (your turn to pick), player_picked, draft_completed, draft_cancelled.
- Endpoints: start, pick, cancel, GET draft state (full state for client resync).
design:
DECIDED (2026-09-26): pick order
- Pick order is a property of the DRAFT, not the session: a session can have several drafts over time (admin may re-draft), and only drafts have an order (direct assignment/proposals don't).
- Support both: pick_order = 'snake' (A,B,B,A,...) | 'alternate' (A,B,A,B,...). Chosen by the admin when starting the draft; default 'snake' (fairer - second captain gets back-to-back picks).
- Backend must know it: the server enforces turns (captain may only pick on their turn), so whose-turn = f(pick_order, current_pick) lives server-side. Keep it a small pure function so more orders / more than two captains stay easy later.
- Storage (in 000001_activity_schema, per project convention - no new migration files):
  activity.session_team_draft(id, session_id, pick_order, status in_progress|completed|cancelled, current_pick, captain_a_id, captain_b_id, started_by, started_at, completed_at)
- Start endpoint takes it: POST /sessions/{id}/draft {captain_ids, pick_order?}; draft_started event carries pick_order; GET draft state returns it.

STILL OPEN: turn timeout (none vs N seconds with auto-skip/auto-pick) - decide before implementing.
Optional/later: 'formed_by' (manual|draft|proposal) on the teams to show how current teams were formed.

DECIDED (2026-09-26, before implementation):
- Turn timeout: NONE in v1. Admin can cancel and restart. (Timeout = later, needs a background job.)
- Captain leaves mid-draft (not_going/maybe, cancels RSVP, removed): draft auto-cancels (draft_cancelled, reason captain_left); existing teams untouched.
- While a draft is in progress: POST /sessions/{id}/teams and direct assign/unassign are rejected (409 draft_in_progress).
- Completion: automatic when no unpicked confirmed attendee remains, or both teams are full (players_per_team). New confirmed attendees mid-draft (RSVP, waitlist promotion, invite) just join the pool; a picked player who leaves is dropped from their draft team; if the last unpicked player leaves, the draft completes.
- Picks live in the draft (session_team_draft_pick) until completion; only then are teams replaced (2 teams, Team A = captain A's side) and team_id written. Cancel never touches teams.
- Turn skipping: if the side whose turn it is is full (players_per_team), the turn passes to the other side.

REVISED (2026-09-26, mobile decisions D1-D9 on the 'Team Formation Backend Asks' page) - supersedes the conflicting points above:
- D1/D2: no max team size (see 6gg.8). No turn skipping for full teams; the draft completes only when everyone going has been picked.
- D5: start requires enough people (D3: 2 x min_players_per_team, or 2) else 409 not_enough_players. Captains must be going.
- D7: joiners enter the pool; leavers leave the pool or their side. If the going count drops below D3 -> draft cancelled, cancelled_reason not_enough_players; teams untouched.
- D8 (replaces 'captain leaving cancels'): captain leaves -> status paused, paused_reason captain_left, that side's captain vacant. Organizer PUT /sessions/{id}/draft/captains {team_position, user_id} names a new captain from that side's picks or from the pool; draft resumes where it stopped. Picks rejected while paused (draft_paused). Organizer can still cancel.
- Naming aligned with mobile: status active|paused|completed|cancelled; cancelled_reason organizer|not_enough_players; team positions 0/1 (not A/B); turn {pick_number, total_picks, team_position, captain_user_id}; turn_order = full order from pick 0 (positions); teams [{position, user_ids}]; version.
- Error codes: not_your_turn, player_not_available, draft_not_active, draft_paused, draft_already_active (also for manual team changes during a draft), invalid_captains, not_enough_players, not_draft_captain, unauthorized.
acceptance_criteria: Draft runs end to end with turn enforcement; concurrent picks are safe; edge cases handled; events emitted; tests for state machine and races
notes: Known edge (2026-09-26, accepted for now): the draft checks the TOTAL going count against D3, not each team's size at completion. Picks alternate so sides differ by at most one, but a picked player dropping out can leave a side below min_players_per_team when the pool is empty (e.g. min 3, 7 going, A=4 B=3, a B pick leaves -> completes 4 vs 2). Handled by the organizer moving someone by hand; mobile shows 'needs N more'. Revisit if mobile wants completion blocked below the minimum.
close_reason: Captain draft per mobile D4-D9: start needs D3, snake/alternate turns enforced under session lock, completes when everyone going is picked, captain leaving pauses + PUT /draft/captains to replace, below D3 cancels, joiners enter pool, manual team changes blocked while running, version + full turn_order, mobile-aligned response and error codes

title: Team proposals and voting: suggest a division, vote, admin closes, winner applied
description:
Proposal aggregate + votes.
- Any confirmed attendee can suggest a full division into teams at any time. Suggesting does NOT reset current teams.
- Every confirmed attendee has one vote across proposals and can change it while voting is open.
- Voting stays open until admin/moderator closes it (no deadline, no auto-close).
- On close: the proposal with most votes is applied automatically (written to team_id). On a tie the admin selects the winner (close is rejected/pending until they choose).
- Always possible to submit new proposals after a close (starts a new voting).
- Validation: proposal must cover only confirmed attendees, respect players_per_team, each attendee in at most one team.
- Edge cases: attendee leaves or is promoted from waitlist while proposals are open (invalidate or adjust proposals - decide), open question whether "keep current teams" is an implicit option, archive vs delete after close.
- Events: proposal_created, vote_cast/changed, voting_closed (winner), tie_requires_admin.
- Endpoints: create proposal, vote, close (with optional winner_proposal_id for ties), list proposals with tallies, GET state.
design:
DECIDED by mobile/product (2026-09-26, 'Team Formation Backend Asks' page D10-D16; D1-D3 in 6gg.8):
- D10: proposals don't need existing teams. A proposal lists teams in order (first = Team A) with their members. If the session already has teams, a proposal must use the same team count; otherwise it sets its own. The winner replaces the current teams (like POST /teams + assignment).
- D11: valid proposal = everyone going on exactly one team, every team >= min_players_per_team, nobody not going. Server validates (invalid_division, ideally with the reason: someone left out, on two teams, not going, team below minimum, wrong team count).
- D12: someone leaving drops out of every proposal, voting continues. If going count < D3 -> voting cancelled (cancelled_reason not_enough_players) and all proposals deleted. Joiners can vote; they are in no proposal and get placed by the organizer after the winner is applied.
- D13: 'keep current teams' is a vote option only when the session has teams; if it wins nothing changes.
- D14: one vote per person going, changeable while open; no deadline; organizer closes.
- D15: tie -> close rejected with 409 tie_requires_winner + tied proposal ids (and keep_current if tied) until winner given; picking it applies and closes.
- D16: proposals and votes are deleted when voting closes (no history; history can be rebuilt from outbox events). A new proposal afterwards starts a new round.

Mobile's suggested API (shape is ours):
  POST /sessions/{id}/proposals {teams: [{user_ids: [...]}, ...]} (anyone going)
  PUT  /sessions/{id}/proposals/vote {proposal_id} | {keep_current: true} (same call to change)
  POST /sessions/{id}/proposals/close {winner_proposal_id?} (organizer)
  GET  /sessions/{id}/proposals -> {voting_status open|closed|cancelled, cancelled_reason, players_going, players_needed, my_vote, votes_cast, eligible_voters, keep_current_votes (null w/o teams), items[{id, author_id, created_at, teams[{position, user_ids}], vote_count}], version}
Error codes: invalid_division, not_enough_players, attendee_not_going, voting_closed, tie_requires_winner, unauthorized; 409 with a specific code for every race (two votes, close vs new proposal).

BACKEND DECISIONS (2026-09-26, Igor):
- Session WITHOUT teams: no minimum applies; a proposal splits everyone going (capacity already caps that). players_needed = team count (1 per team). Session WITH teams: players_needed = team count x min_players_per_team (D3).
- Team count per round: the first proposal of a round fixes it (or the session's team count when teams exist); later proposals in that round must match (wrong_team_count).
- Teams replaced while voting is open (POST /teams again): the round is cancelled, cancelled_reason teams_replaced, proposals deleted.
- Draft and voting are mutually exclusive: starting a draft while voting is open -> 409 voting_open; proposing while a draft runs -> 409 draft_already_active.
- A leaver dropping out can leave a proposal's team below the minimum; it can still win - the organizer fixes it by hand (same as the draft edge). Only the total (players_needed) cancels voting.
- Storage: a voting round row per round (status, reasons, team count, version, result) is kept after close so GET can show closed/cancelled; its proposals, members and votes are deleted when it ends (D16).
acceptance_criteria: Proposals and voting work end to end; tie resolved by admin; winner applied automatically; re-suggesting never resets teams; roster-change edge cases handled; tests
close_reason: Team proposals and voting per mobile D10-D16: propose/vote/close/get, round fixes team count, D11 validation with reasons, keep-current option, tie needs organizer pick, winner replaces teams, proposals/votes deleted on close, leavers dropped, below-needed and teams-replaced cancel, draft/voting mutually exclusive, all under session lock
